verdicts.actual_behavior: In exa.agent(), the wall-clock budget is not what the docstring promises. (1) The POST create call (line 2404, `timeout=min(timeout,30)`) runs BEFORE `deadline = time.time() + timeout` (line 2409), so the create call's elapsed time is entirely outside the budget — every call pays create-time on top of `timeout`. The function still behaves correctly otherwise — it returns the run on success and raises ExaError "did not finish within {timeout}s" on timeout — so the OUTPUT is right; only the latency bound the docstring promises ("Max total wall-clock seconds to wait for completion", line 2366) is violated. Typical-magnitude caveat: create and status GETs usually return in well under their caps, so the overshoot is small in the happy path and only reaches the worst case under slow network/server conditions.
